title: Claim: unit-tests-run-fast
body: Unit tests on isolated components run in milliseconds, not seconds, because they avoid I/O.

title: Claim: hermetic-tests-never-touch-external-services
body: Hermetic tests mock all external dependencies: databases, networks, file systems, caches.

title: Claim: dependency-injection-enables-mocking
body: Functions that take dependencies as parameters (not globals) can be tested with mock objects.

title: Claim: markers-enable-selective-execution
body: @pytest.mark.unit and @pytest.mark.integration allow running only a subset of tests before commit.

title: Claim: mocking-is-for-external-io
body: Mock external services (HTTP, database, file I/O); test real logic with real domain objects.

title: Complexity: unit test (mock dependency)
body:
**O(1) milliseconds**

isolated component, no I/O

title: Complexity: unit test setup (fixture with monkeypatch)
body:
**O(1) setup time**

in-memory fixture; minimal allocation

title: Complexity: mock assertion (verify call count, args)
body:
**O(1)**

recorded in-memory; no I/O

title: Complexity: unit test with parametrize (@pytest.mark.parametrize)
body:
**O(n) for n inputs**

same test run multiple times; linear in test count

title: Complexity: test collection (pytest discovery)
body:
**O(n) where n is number of test files**

imports all test modules; linear scan

title: Complexity: parallel unit tests (pytest-xdist, -n auto)
body:
**O(n/p) where p is number of processes**

ideal speedup if tests are independent

title: Q1: Why should unit tests avoid calling external services like d
body:
A. External services are always slower, so tests must be fast
B. Tests should be hermetic: deterministic, fast, and runnable in any order or location
C. External services are not available in the test environment
D. All of the above

**B.** Hermetic tests are isolated and reproducible. They run in milliseconds, in any order, and don't depend on network or service availability.

title: Q2: Which pytest marker should a fast, isolated test declare?
body:
A. @pytest.mark.integration
B. @pytest.mark.unit
C. @pytest.mark.slow
D. @pytest.mark.skip

**B.** @pytest.mark.unit tags fast, isolated component tests. Markers allow running only unit tests before commit with `pytest -m unit`.

title: Q3: What does unittest.mock.MagicMock.side_effect do?
body:
A. Records how many times the mock was called
B. Defines the return value of the mock
C. Raises an exception or returns a value when the mock is called
D. Prevents the mock from being called more than once

**C.** side_effect can be an exception (raises it) or a callable (calls it). This lets tests trigger error paths without raising real errors.

title: Q4: In dependency injection, what is passed to the function bein
body:
A. The real external service
B. A mock object that simulates the service
C. A stub that returns a default value
D. Both mock and stub objects

**B.** Mocks replace real dependencies in tests, allowing control over inputs and verification of behavior without side effects.

title: Q5: What does @pytest.mark.parametrize do?
body:
A. Skips a test until it passes
B. Runs a test multiple times with different inputs
C. Marks a test as slow or expensive
D. Enables parallel test execution

**B.** Parametrize runs the same test function with different arguments, specified as a list of tuples. This keeps tests DRY.

title: 1. Isolate a function from a database dependency
body:
**Pattern**: dependency injection (pass mock as parameter or fixture)

**Why**: A function that queries a database cannot run fast or repeatably. Mock the database to return test data.

**Python**: `unittest.mock.MagicMock or pytest-mock`

title: 2. Test error handling without triggering real errors
body:
**Pattern**: mock.side_effect = ExceptionType() to trigger error paths

**Why**: Testing error paths without actually raising them lets tests run fast and verify both success and failure.

**Python**: `unittest.mock.MagicMock.side_effect`

title: 3. Verify a function logs the correct message
body:
**Pattern**: pass mock logger to function; assert mock.assert_called_with(...)

**Why**: Capturing logging without side effects; verify the function called log with the right args.

**Python**: `unittest.mock.patch, pytest-mock, capsys`

title: 4. Test a class that depends on an external service
body:
**Pattern**: constructor injection (pass mock in __init__); mock returns test data

**Why**: Classes that call external APIs must be testable without hitting the network; inject mocks.

**Python**: `unittest.mock.MagicMock, @pytest.fixture`

title: 5. Run the same test on 10 different inputs
body:
**Pattern**: @pytest.mark.parametrize with list of (input, expected)

**Why**: Avoids copy-pasting the same test 10 times; DRY principle for test cases.

**Python**: `@pytest.mark.parametrize decorator`

title: Signal: Verify a single function's behavior given various inputs
body:
**Structure**: function under test + mock dependencies + assertions

**Requirement**: O(1) milliseconds, no external calls

**Python**: `@pytest.fixture, unittest.mock.MagicMock, pytest-mock`

**Example**: test_branch_from_result_whitespace_frozen; verify branch_from_result('   ') is None

title: Signal: Test a class constructor, field assignment, and simple metho
body:
**Structure**: instantiate class, set fields, call methods, assert results

**Requirement**: O(1), no I/O or network

**Python**: `@pytest.fixture for object construction, capsys for stdout capture`

**Example**: test_error_initialization; verify FleetError('msg').message == 'msg'

title: Signal: Test error handling and exception messages
body:
**Structure**: pytest.raises(ExceptionType), assert error details

**Requirement**: O(1), verify exception type and message text

**Python**: `pytest.raises context manager`

**Example**: test_policy_violation_includes_rule_id; verify PolicyViolation('X').rule_id == 'X'

title: Signal: Verify function calls to a mocked dependency (call count, ar
body:
**Structure**: mock.assert_called_once_with(...) or mock.call_count assertions

**Requirement**: O(1), inspect mock call history

**Python**: `unittest.mock.MagicMock, pytest-mock`

**Example**: verify a logger was called with the correct message

title: Signal: Run the same test on multiple inputs (parametrize)
body:
**Structure**: @pytest.mark.parametrize with list of (input, expected) tuples

**Requirement**: O(n) where n is number of inputs, but DRY

**Python**: `@pytest.mark.parametrize decorator`

**Example**: test_json_parse with [('{"a":1}', {'a': 1}), ('bad', ValueError)]
